title: Blackberry pie, double-crust
subtitle: Late-summer blackberries under a golden shortcrust lid
excerpt: Blackberry pie with a buttery double-crust pastry and a filling that sets jammy and deep purple around the berries. Wild blackberries from hedgerows work best; cultivated berries are reliable but milder. Serve warm with clotted cream or vanilla ice cream.
sourceNotes: Blackberry pie is documented in British and American baking tradition. Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), Project Gutenberg #10136, includes bramble-fruit preparations. The double-crust shortcrust format is the British standard for soft-fruit pies.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked and cooled, wrapped tightly, for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and warm at 170°C for 15 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pastry can be made 2 days ahead. The filling holds overnight in the fridge.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional oven for first 20 minutes; drop to 180°C for final 25 to 30 minutes; fan 180°C then 160°C

content.text: Blackberry pie is dark, jammy, and slightly seedy, sweet with a good edge of sharpness. Wild berries are more acidic than cultivated ones. If using wild hedgerow berries, add an extra 30 g of sugar to the filling.

attrs.prepNote: fresh or frozen (defrost and drain if frozen)

content.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour, 30 g caster sugar, and a pinch of salt until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add 5 to 6 tablespoons cold water and bring to a dough. Divide two thirds / one third for the base and lid. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.

Toss the blackberries gently with 180 g caster sugar, 35 g cornflour, the lemon juice, and the cinnamon. The cornflour will absorb the berry juices during baking and prevent the filling from flooding out when the pie is cut.

Roll the larger piece of pastry to 4 mm and line a 23 cm pie dish with a 2 cm overhang. Pile in the blackberry filling, it will look too full but sinks during baking. Roll the remaining pastry to a lid and press over the filling. Crimp the edges. Cut five or six small vents in the lid. Brush with beaten egg and scatter over a little extra caster sugar.

Bake at 200°C (conventional) for 20 minutes, then drop to 180°C for a further 25 to 30 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the blackberry filling is bubbling through the vents. Rest for 30 minutes before serving. Serve warm with clotted cream or ice cream.
